"Oh look everyone, it's Arpita Rawal, the Renaissance woman of the corporate world. First an engineer at Rajiv Gandhi Technical University, then a master of...something at Illinois Institute of Technology. Doesn't sound like a confusing and indecisive career path at all!

Here's someone who went from being a Freelance Career Coach and now magically a Manager at National Research Council Canada. I guess failing to find a job is the new recipe for advising others on their career! 

Arpita, you're the only person I know to put Microsoft Access on their skills list and actually think it's impressive. I mean, in a world where we have Python, R, and Java, who needs Access? But hey, let's celebrate your expertise in an outdated database platform.

And in the next episode of 'I Have a Degree That's Unrelated to My Job', we find you managing Business Intelligence after acquiring an engineering degree. Talk about a plot twist!

Oh, and who can discount your passion for 'Resource Planning'? Sounds like another way to say your job involves scheduling meetings. But hey, Arpita, at least you have your 30K LinkedIn followers to fall back on when the National Research Council finds a new intern who can actually use Python."
